root_cause: FIRST audio-channel run (gemini-3.1-flash-lite, TTS sim user + ASR). Same sim passes 3/3 on text. Both failing runs are audio-channel artifacts, not an agent logic bug. Run 1: ASR transcribed the sim user's spoken 'Bluebird' as the two-word 'Blue Bird', so verify_passcode was called with passcode='Blue Bird' which fails the exact (strip+lower) compare against the stored 'Bluebird' -- this happened on all 3 attempts, so the agent correctly escalated to an operator after 3 failures and never reached call_cancel_alarm / the no-active-alarm message. Run 2 is a DIFFERENT, unrelated audio-instability failure: after a SUCCESSFUL lookup_accounts_by_caller call (returned the 3 branches), the agent spuriously said 'I am having trouble accessing your account details' and called end_session(reason='error', session_escalated=True) at turn 3 -- a model bail-out despite valid tool output. Deeper actionable cause across the cluster is the ASR-fragile compound-word passcode 'Bluebird'; run 2's spurious-error bail is sporadic audio-model flakiness. Pass rate 1/3 (intermediate) confirms non-deterministic audio variance rather than a broken agent.

Is this sim-user behavior? YES for run 1: TTS-spoken 'Bluebird' mis-ASR'd to 'Blue Bird' is a sim-user/channel artifact, not agent logic
Is the sim config robust to audio? NO: the passcode fixture 'Bluebird' is a compound word that ASR routinely splits into two tokens, guaranteeing verify_passcode mismatch in audio

Is the agent wrong? Run 1 NO (correct retry+escalation behavior given mismatched ASR input). Run 2 = sporadic model bail-out after a successful tool call (audio flakiness), not a reproducible logic bug
fix_summary_one_line: Audio variance: ASR split 'Bluebird'->'Blue Bird' broke passcode verify (run1) and a spurious post-lookup end_session error (run2). Primary fix: make the passcode ASR-robust -- either swap the sim fixture 'Bluebird' for a single-token word (e.g. 'Sunset'/'Harbor') in simulations.yaml + the verify_passcode mock, OR normalize internal whitespace in verify_passcode (passcode.replace(' ','').strip().lower()) so 'Blue Bird' matches 'Bluebird'. Run2's spurious-error bail is audio model flakiness -- accept as audio variance / re-run.
